title: BDC Business Loans in Canada: Rates, Eligibility, and How to Apply
excerpt: BDC lends directly to Canadian businesses, up to $350,000 online. Here are the real eligibility rules, how its rates are set, approval timelines, and when a faster alternative lender makes more sense.
content:
BDC business loans come directly from the Business Development Bank of Canada, a federal Crown corporation, not through your own bank. Its online Small Business Loan lends up to $350,000 to profitable Canadian companies with at least 24 months of history, at a floating rate the Bank sets for your file.

BDC is often the cheapest growth capital a small business can get. It is also stricter and slower than many private lenders, and it turns down companies that are young, unprofitable, or thin on records. This guide covers what BDC actually offers, who qualifies, how its pricing works, and what to do if BDC is not the right fit. All figures come from BDC's own pages; confirm current terms with BDC before you apply.

What is BDC, and how is it different from your bank?

BDC is the Business Development Bank of Canada, a Crown corporation owned by the federal government and dedicated to Canadian entrepreneurs. Unlike the Canada Small Business Financing Program, where your own bank makes the loan and Ottawa guarantees part of it, BDC lends its own money and makes its own decision.

That has two practical effects. First, you apply to BDC directly, online or through a BDC account manager, not at your branch. Second, because BDC exists to support businesses rather than maximize profit, its terms are often more patient than a commercial bank's, with longer amortizations and interest-only start periods. For a side-by-side of the two government routes, see our guide to CSBFP vs BDC loans.

What types of BDC loans are available?

BDC offers several financing lines, not one product. The online Small Business Loan is the fastest and most self-serve; larger or specialized financing is arranged with an advisor.

  • Small Business Loan: BDC's online term loan, up to $350,000, for everyday growth costs.
  • Working capital loans: to fund operations, cash-flow gaps, or a specific project without tying up your own cash.
  • Equipment and commercial real estate financing: term loans to buy machinery, vehicles, land, or buildings, usually amortized over the life of the asset.
  • Technology and intangibles financing: for software, digital projects, and other assets a traditional bank is reluctant to secure.
  • Targeted programs: BDC periodically runs focused streams, such as inclusive-entrepreneurship lending and liquidity support for businesses hit by tariffs. Availability and terms change, so check bdc.ca.

Most of the numbers below describe the online Small Business Loan, because it is the product most small businesses compare against private lenders.

How much can you borrow, and what can you use it for?

BDC's online Small Business Loan runs up to $350,000, and BDC sets the approved amount from its analysis of your request. The product splits into two tiers with different rules: loans up to $100,000, and loans from $100,000 to $350,000.

The loan is meant for daily operations and growth projects rather than hard assets alone. BDC lists uses such as buying inventory, developing products, paying suppliers, hiring and training staff, running marketing campaigns, improving energy efficiency, earning industry certifications, and entering new markets. If you are buying a specific large asset like equipment or property, BDC's equipment or real-estate financing (or a CSBFP loan through your bank) is often the better fit.

Who qualifies for a BDC Small Business Loan?

You generally need a revenue-generating Canadian business that has operated for at least two years and is currently profitable. The exact bar depends on how much you borrow.

RequirementUp to $100,000$100,000 to $350,000
Annual revenueAt least $100,000At least $250,000
Time in business24 months (12 to 24 possible, with longer approval and possible extra fees)24 months of financial statements
ProfitabilityCurrently profitableCurrently profitable
Personal credit score600 or higher600 or higher
LocationCanadaCanada

Source: BDC, Small Business Loan. Meeting these criteria does not guarantee approval. BDC also weighs your cash flow, overall business potential, and management, not only the numbers in the table.

The pattern is clear: BDC is built for established, profitable businesses. If you are pre-revenue, under two years old, or still working back to profitability, the online loan will likely be out of reach, and you will need BDC's start-up financing, a CSBFP loan, or a private alternative.

What interest rate does BDC charge?

BDC does not publish a fixed rate. Its Small Business Loan uses a floating base rate plus a variance the Bank sets from your personal and business profile, so the rate differs for every borrower.

Two things follow from that. First, a stronger file (more history, higher revenue, clean credit) earns a smaller premium, so pricing rewards exactly the businesses that already qualify easily. Second, because the base rate floats, your payment can move up or down over the life of the loan if rates change. BDC does not offer a fixed rate on this online product. Historically, development-bank pricing has sat at a premium over prime to reflect the added risk BDC takes on; for a current quote, ask BDC directly rather than relying on third-party estimates.

Whatever rate you are offered, compare lenders on total cost rather than the headline rate. Fees, the amortization length, and any interest-only period all change what you actually pay. The True North small business loans overview explains how those pieces fit together.

What are the fees, terms, and repayment schedule?

BDC's terms are more flexible than most banks', especially on the smaller tier. Here are the posted terms for the online Small Business Loan.

TermUp to $100,000$100,000 to $350,000
Application feeNoneCertain fees apply
Prepayment feeNoneNot specified
Interest-only startUp to 6 monthsUp to 12 months
Amortization (repayment term)5 yearsUp to 8 years
Rate typeFloating (base rate + variance)Floating (base rate + variance)

Source: BDC, Small Business Loan. The interest-only start can be useful: it lets you deploy the capital and generate revenue before full principal-and-interest payments begin. The no-fee, no-prepayment-penalty structure under $100,000 also makes early repayment painless if your cash flow improves.

How long does BDC take, and how do you apply?

BDC is reasonably fast for a bank, though not as fast as online private lenders. It states approval in under 10 days for loans up to $100,000, and under 30 days for loans from $100,000 to $350,000, subject to conditions. After approval, funds can arrive within a few days, often less than a week.

Applying follows four basic steps:

  1. Check eligibility and gather documents. Have your business financials for the last 24 months, recent bank statements, and your personal credit position ready.
  2. Apply online or with an account manager. The smaller loan is designed to be completed online; larger requests usually involve a BDC advisor.
  3. Underwriting and verification. BDC reviews your revenue, profitability, cash flow, and credit, and may ask follow-up questions.
  4. Approval and funding. Once approved and any conditions are met, BDC disburses the funds.

To speed things up, respond to document requests the same day and make sure your financial statements are current and consistent with your bank activity.

BDC vs a matched private lender: which is right for you?

BDC and a private alternative lender solve different problems. BDC gives cheaper, longer money to businesses that can wait and can clear its bar. A matched alternative lender gives fast, flexible money to businesses that cannot, at a higher price. Neither is universally better.

BDC Small Business LoanMatched private lender
Loan size$10,000 to $350,000Roughly $5,000 to $800,000
Who lendsBDC directlyA private lender matched to your profile
Typical costLower (floating base rate + variance)Higher, varies widely by risk and product
Time in business24 months, must be profitableOften as little as 6 months accepted
SpeedApproval in about 10 to 30 daysOften approval in 24 to 48 hours
Best forEstablished, profitable growth plansUrgent needs, younger or thin-file businesses

If you comfortably meet BDC's rules and your need is not urgent, BDC is usually the smart first call on cost. If you are under two years old, not yet profitable, or racing a deadline, a private lender may be the only realistic option. For the full trade-off, read bank vs alternative lender.

When does an alternative lender make more sense?

When BDC's answer is no, or when waiting costs more than the extra interest. A private alternative lender often funds in a day or two and accepts shorter operating histories, which matters in specific situations:

  • You have a signed contract or purchase order you cannot fill without cash now.
  • You are under 24 months in business with steady deposits but no profit yet.
  • A missed season, a supplier discount, or a lost contract would cost more than the interest.

It rarely makes sense to borrow expensive money just to cover ongoing losses. If you do go the alternative route, get the annual percentage rate in writing, compare at least two offers, and make sure the capital earns more than it costs.

Frequently asked questions

Does BDC lend directly, or through my bank?

Directly. BDC is a federal Crown corporation that lends its own money and makes its own credit decision. That is the opposite of the Canada Small Business Financing Program, where your own bank issues the loan and the government guarantees part of it.

What credit score do I need for a BDC Small Business Loan?

BDC lists a minimum personal credit score of 600 for both loan tiers. A score at or above that does not guarantee approval; BDC also reviews your revenue, profitability, cash flow, and management.

Can a start-up get a BDC loan?

Not the standard online Small Business Loan, which expects about 24 months in business and current profits. Businesses operating 12 to 24 months may sometimes qualify, with longer approval and possible extra fees. BDC does offer separate start-up financing, and start-ups can also pursue a CSBFP loan through a bank.

How much can I borrow from BDC?

The online Small Business Loan ranges up to $350,000, with a typical minimum of $10,000. Loans up to $100,000 have lighter revenue requirements and faster approval; loans from $100,000 to $350,000 require at least $250,000 in annual revenue and 24 months of financial statements. BDC's other products can fund larger amounts through an advisor.

What interest rate will BDC charge me?

BDC does not publish a fixed rate. It charges a floating base rate plus a variance set from your personal and business profile, so pricing varies by borrower and can change over the life of the loan. Ask BDC for a personalized quote.

How long does BDC take to fund a loan?

BDC states approval in under 10 days for loans up to $100,000 and under 30 days for loans from $100,000 to $350,000, subject to conditions, with funds typically available within a few days of approval. Private alternative lenders are often faster, sometimes 24 to 48 hours.
